title: MaxSup: Overcoming Representation Collapse in Label Smoothing

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'While a direct closed-form expression is complex due to the softmax normalization, the effective Label Smoothing loss can be approximated by: LLS ≈ α ( zgt − (1/K) ∑_{k=1}^K zk ) − log \sum_{j=1}^K e^{z_j}'. However, the accompanying derivation in Appendix B (Proof of Theorem 3.3) shows that the exact closed-form expression is L_LS = α (z_gt - (1/K) Σ_k z_k), with no extraneous log-sum-exp term. The expression in Theorem 3.3 is therefore mathematically incorrect and contradicts the paper's own proof; it is not an approximation but a mistaken formula.

The text states: 'Although all regularizers typically decrease $\bar{d}_{\text{within}}$ compared to the baseline, Logit Penalty occasionally displays increased $\bar{d}_{\text{within}}$ and $R^2$ values, inconsistent with prior results. This anomaly likely results from unstable estimation ...'. However, in Table 2, Logit Penalty's $\bar{d}_{\text{within}}$ values are 0.284 (train) and 0.314 (val), both lower than the baseline values of 0.311 and 0.331. No increase in $\bar{d}_{\text{within}}$ is observed; the claim of 'occasionally displays increased $\bar{d}_{\text{within}}$' is not supported by the presented data and appears to be a misreading of the table.

Section 4.3 says: 'we adopt the UperNet [40] architecture with a DeiT-Small backbone, trained on ADE20K. ... using the widely adopted MMSegmentation framework [6].' Reference [6] is Gao et al., 'Towards a better understanding of label smoothing in neural machine translation', which has no connection to the MMSegmentation software. The correct citation for MMSegmentation would be a different reference, e.g., the OpenMMLab mmsegmentation repository. This misattribution misleads the reader about the source of the framework.
